what: Brookfield Corporation is an owner and manager of real assets. Through Brookfield Asset Management and its listed affiliates it owns infrastructure, renewable power, real estate and private equity holdings, and manages money for institutions on top of that.
customers: Pension funds, sovereign wealth funds and insurers investing in its funds, plus tenants and customers of the assets it owns.
money: fees on capital managed for institutions
annuity and insurance assets invested in its own strategies
renewable power, infrastructure, real estate and private equity
moat: Decades of experience owning hard assets, which gives it access to deals and the credibility to raise very large funds from institutions.
risks: Consolidated debt of about $282 billion looks enormous, though most is non-recourse at the asset level
Reported revenue fell about 13% last year
The structure of listed affiliates is complex and hard to value
Office real estate holdings have fallen in value
opportunities: Fee-bearing capital grows as institutions allocate more to infrastructure and private credit
Insurance assets provide permanent capital to invest
Analysts see substantial upside to the current share price
watch: Fee-bearing capital growth and distributable earnings per share.
